decisions.reason: The particle therapy water phantom builds directly on the firm's long scanning-phantom and dosimetry expertise, and its slow clinical adoption cycle means early feedback is still being absorbed and fed into refinements, which favours keeping it.

Small volume chambers are core detector know-how that the firm's accredited calibration lab and physicists can evaluate and improve, though the earlier pruning of chamber lines adds some risk of portfolio consolidation.
It serves growing small-field dosimetry demand on the same knowledge base, but its overlap with Product B makes it the more likely candidate if the firm consolidates its chamber range.
Thimble chambers are a long-standing core competence with long regulatory and clinical life cycles and established calibration routines, so withdrawal within a year is unlikely.
